text:
Liam: Aurora Labs disputed INV-2026-08-02. They say a deployment rollback caused duplicate metering across regions and resulted in burst charges. Requesting refund + SLA credit.

Fiona: can we get commit attribution for 2026-08-01 22:10-22:30 UTC? customer claims traffic should have stayed on aurora-dedicated-01.

Anika: pulling logs. quick look: deployment rollback re-registered old node ids without clearing previous meter tags. That caused the same requests to be counted against both region-us and region-eu pools for ~9 minutes.

Anika: snippet: ```meters:
2026-08-01T22:12Z -> aurora-dedicated-01 (us)
2026-08-01T22:12Z -> aurora-dedicated-01 (eu)
```
Estimated overcharge = $4,220.

Finance-bot: Policy: refunds > $5k need director + legal signoff. Under $5k, ops can approve with ticket documentation.

Liam: charge ids: CHG-14001, CHG-14002. Recon worksheet in ticket #4477 with per-minute breakdown and logs. Recommend refund of $4,220 and a 3% SLA credit as goodwill.

Fiona: engineering fix in ops: ensure meter tags are deduped on node re-registration. Patch deployed to canary. ETA full rollout: 6h. ops-bot: created revert-guard flag.

Ops-bot: deployment log: revert-guard enabled at 2026-08-02T01:05Z. Monitoring shows no duplicate meter events on canary.

Anika: Because amount < $5k, I can approve cash refund. I'll attach logs and the mitigation note to ticket #4477 and process refund.

Liam: please run `/process-refund CHG-14001,CHG-14002 amount=4220 ticket=4477 note="Aurora Labs - duplicate metering due to rollback"` and send customer note.

Fiona: I'll follow up with a short postmortem and add a test to CI to simulate node re-registration.

Sam: Thanks for the fast turnaround. Please include the remediation details in the customer note.
